top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P002) has the most stable and nameable centre: memory, the body and dream built into a metaphysical architecture across poetry and prose over decades, with an unambiguous single author, language and citation scope. On public knowledge, the project in Blinding and Solenoid is distinctive and sustained, and a citation naming poetry and prose together does not have to rest on the largest novels alone. The margin over Carson (P001) is narrow and rests on weighting unity and scale of project slightly above breadth of formal reinvention. Carson's case is strong and her supporters' narrowing of the citation to original verse novel, elegy and essay answers most of my delimitation concern. I hold my preference with real uncertainty: I cannot assess the Romanian directly, I rely on translations and public accounts, and I cannot verify whether the late work extends or repeats the earlier project or whether the long novels lapse into excess. Both leading candidates also carry an unverified later-work question. Opening and round-1 support counts are not treated as evidence of merit. P000 is ranked last because both leading proposals show substantial literary achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my scholarship on the fragment, poetic nihilism, exile literature and Celan overlaps thematically with Carson, Adonis and Cărtărescu, but that is context and not a tie to any candidate. As chair I wrote the round-1 summary, a disclosed potential influence on framing.
